Add the Estimated Post-Transplant Survival score

Source: R/add_epts.R
add_epts.Rd

Computes the raw Estimated Post-Transplant Survival (EPTS) value for adult kidney candidates or recipients from Standard Analysis File (SAF) columns and maps it to the EPTS score, a percentile from 0 to 100, with an OPTN mapping table (see optn_mapping_tables).

Usage

add_epts(
  df,
  at = c("listing", "transplant"),
  table = "latest",
  unknown_diabetes = c("na", "no"),
  missing_dialysis_date = c("status", "zero"),
  adults_only = TRUE,
  epts_col = "EPTS",
  raw_col = "EPTS_RAW",
  return_terms = FALSE
)

Arguments

df

A data frame of candidates or recipients, one row each.

at

Score the candidate at "listing" (default) or at "transplant".

table

Which mapping table to use: "latest" (default), the newest stored table; "in_force", for each row the table OPTN was using on the date scored; or a table label such as "2018". For "in_force", each table's start date is OPTN's published date where one exists (2024-05-29 and 2025-05-21); otherwise it is June 1 of the year after the snapshot, the deadline in OPTN Policy 8.4.B, which is a convention. Rows with no stored table in force get a missing score, with a warning. The dates and their basis are in optn_mapping_tables$effective.

unknown_diabetes

How to treat unknown diabetes status (code 998). "na" (default) gives a missing score. "no" counts it as no diabetes; this is a convention some analyses use, not part of the OPTN definition.

missing_dialysis_date

How to treat a missing dialysis start date. "status" (default) counts it as 0 years when the dialysis status column says the candidate was not on dialysis (code 1), and otherwise gives a missing score. "zero" always counts it as 0 years, a convention.

adults_only

If TRUE (default), candidates under 18 get a missing score: OPTN assigns EPTS to adults only.

epts_col, raw_col

Names of the output columns for the score and the raw value.

return_terms

If TRUE, also add a list-column EPTS_terms with each row's inputs.

Value

df with two new columns. The score column carries an optn_table attribute with the table label used for each row.

Details

EPTS uses four factors: age, current diabetes, any prior solid organ transplant, and years on dialysis. They are read from these columns (labelled factors from apply_srtr_factors() also work):

Factorat = "listing"at = "transplant"
Date scoredCAN_LISTING_DTREC_TX_DT
AgeCAN_AGE_IN_MONTHS_AT_LISTING / 12REC_AGE_IN_MONTHS_AT_TX / 12
Dialysis startCAN_DIAL_DTREC_DIAL_DT
Dialysis statusCAN_DIALREC_DIAL_TY

Diabetes comes from CAN_DIAB_TY (1 no; 2 to 5 yes; 998 unknown), or CAN_DIAB when that column is absent. A prior solid organ transplant is any value above 0 (or Y) among the organ columns *_PREV_HL, *_PREV_HR, *_PREV_IN, *_PREV_KI, *_PREV_KP, *_PREV_LI, *_PREV_LU and *_PREV_PA that are present: REC_PREV_* at transplant when any are present, otherwise CAN_PREV_*. It is none when every column present is 0 (or N), and missing otherwise. CAN_PREV_TX is used only when no organ column is present, because it may count non-organ transplants. The dictionary gives these columns no format, so whether they are counts or flags is read the same way.

OPTN measures age in fractional years from the date of birth. SAFs carry age in whole months, so age here is months / 12, which can differ from OPTN's by up to one month (a raw EPTS difference of at most 0.004). Years on dialysis is the days from dialysis start to the date scored, divided by 365.25, and 0 if dialysis starts later.

References

OPTN. A Guide to Calculating and Interpreting the Estimated Post-Transplant Survival (EPTS) Score Used in the Kidney Allocation System. Updated 2026-04-07 (formula and worked examples).

Examples

candidates <- data.frame(
  CAN_AGE_IN_MONTHS_AT_LISTING = c(600, 300),
  CAN_LISTING_DT = as.Date(c("2025-01-01", "2025-01-01")),
  CAN_DIAL_DT = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", NA)),
  CAN_DIAL = c(2, 1),
  CAN_DIAB_TY = c(1, 3),
  CAN_PREV_KI = c("N", "Y")
)
add_epts(candidates)
#>   CAN_AGE_IN_MONTHS_AT_LISTING CAN_LISTING_DT CAN_DIAL_DT CAN_DIAL CAN_DIAB_TY
#> 1                          600     2025-01-01  2020-01-01        2           1
#> 2                          300     2025-01-01        <NA>        1           3
#>   CAN_PREV_KI EPTS_RAW EPTS
#> 1           N 1.739512   28
#> 2           Y 1.205000   14
